Our Story

Two families, two traditions, one celebration

From Richmond to the Blue Ridge, with family joining from across the country and from India — we can't wait to celebrate in the mountains with the people we love most.

The Big Day

Ceremony & reception in the mountains

The afternoonCeremony

The Ceremony

An outdoor ceremony under the mandap with the Blue Ridge behind us, honoring both of our traditions. Start time comes with the full schedule.

The eveningReception

Dinner & Reception

Cocktail hour with chaat and pani puri, then a full evening of it: steak and glazed salmon alongside an Indian buffet, two desserts and cake, open bar, and a DJ until the stars are out.

Before you come

A few kind notes

UnderfootThe walk

Mountain ground

We are marrying outdoors, high in the Blue Ridge, and the ground is mountain ground — grass and gravel, sloping and uneven in places, with a short walk between the parking, the ceremony and the lodge. Flat soles or a block heel will carry you through the day far more happily than a fine heel. Bring something warm for the evening; the air turns once the sun is off the ridge.

If steps or distance are difficult for anyone in your party, tell us when you reply and we will make sure you are looked after on the day.

Your partyAs invited

Seats are held by name

Your card tells you how many seats are reserved in your name, and your reply names them one by one. The mountain holds only so many, so we kindly ask that those be the seats that come. Children and guests are very welcome wherever the invitation includes them — and where it does, we have said so plainly.

If you are unsure, or hoping to bring someone, do ask us. We would far rather you asked than wondered.

AttireTwo colours

Anything but red or white

Sharon will wear red for the ceremony and white for the evening, as both of our traditions ask of a bride. So that those two moments stay hers, we kindly ask that guests choose any other colour. Everything else is open to you — and autumn on the mountain rather invites the warm end of the wardrobe.
